title: Projective and simple Grothendieck classes in a small non-semisimple block
statement: Take $F=\mathbb C$, $\xi=-1$ (so $e=2$), level one $\Lambda_0$ and $d=2$. Then $H^\Lambda_2=H_{\mathbb C,-1}(S_2)$ with $T_1^2=-2T_1-1$, i.e. $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra is $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ with $t=T_1+1$, a local algebra whose unique simple is $D=\mathbb C$ with $t$ acting as $0$, and whose regular module is the unique indecomposable projective $P=H^\Lambda_2$. Both partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$ convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$; its transported grading has $\deg t=2$ (the KLR block is the rank-two $e=2$ block $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg y_2=2$). The graded Specht modules are the one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is $0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so $$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$ The restricted label is $(1,1)$ (since $(1,1)$ is $2$-restricted and $(2)$ is not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and $\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence under the transported identifications of [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] $$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$ The graded Cartan pairing of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] has $h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$, while the graded composition multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ (ungraded value $2$). Thus the projective class $[P]$ is not a simple class, and the two bases are dual to each other under $h$ without being equal as classes. All computations are finite and explicit; choice is inherited only through the transported identifications cited.
strategy: Compute in the algebra: $T_1^2=(\xi-1)T_1+\xi=-2T_1-1$ gives $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ is local with radical $(t)$ and unique simple $D=\mathbb C$, and the regular module is the unique indecomposable projective because a local algebra has a unique simple and its regular module is projective; the graded composition series follows from $tP\cong D\{2\}$ (multiplication by $t$ shifts degree by $2$) and $P\cong D\oplus tP$ as graded vector spaces. The block statement uses the residue-content computation: nodes of $(2)$ have residues $0,1$ and nodes of $(1,1)$ have residues $0,-1\equiv1$, so both lie in the block of content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1=\alpha_1+\alpha_0$; the transported grading is [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock identities are the explicit $e=2$ computation of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]] (its recorded $e=2$ example), the graded Specht degrees are read from the degree recursion of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] (the unique tableau of $(2)$ has degree $d_A(2)=1$: the addable $1$-node $(2,1)$ lies strictly below the removable node $(1,2)$, and there is no removable $1$-node below it), and the projective/simple identifications are [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]]. The pairing values are read from $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,D)=\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,P)=1+q^2$ (endomorphisms are the identity and multiplication by $t$, of degree $2$). No choice.
